conviction_note: Sum of four sized findings (+2.0, +3.0, -1.5, -1.0); the ~20% option-implied move is an artefact of a 67%-of-mid ATM spread on 6,544 total contracts, so I anchored on the 6-print history (median abs 11.5%, mean +1.25%, last three +3.7/+14.6/+16.5) and let a stuck 25%-of-float short base plus a Q4 revenue bar that sits below the year's own run-rate tip a coin-flip fundamental modestly positive.

findings.finding: FY26 has declined at a remarkably steady rate (-11.1% Q1, -9.5% Q2, -11.6% Q3; nine months $1,210.4m, -10.3%), yet the -10%/-12% full-year guide implies Q4 revenue of $272.9m-$306.6m against a $336.6m Q4 FY25 base, i.e. -8.9% to -18.9%: simple extrapolation of the year's own run-rate lands ~$300m, at the favourable end, while a $1.50bn full-year consensus requires ~$290m (-14%), a 3-4pp step-down no quarter of FY26 has produced.
findings.why_not_priced: Only two analysts publish on this $230m name and no earnings preview exists on the wire for 10 September (searched businesswire, stocktitan, marketbeat, gurufocus). The single reason to model a Q4 step-down is management's one sentence that the marketing-mix shift 'is expected to impact our fourth quarter performance', which has been taken at face value rather than tested against the arithmetic. If the market had done the arithmetic, the guide's low end would be visibly discounted rather than being where the published full-year consensus sits.
findings.independence: The Q4 FY25 base of $336.6m and FY25 total of $1.69bn come from a different document, the 2025-09-04 year-end release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1084869/000143774925028327/ex_858981.htm . Industry demand for the quarter's single holiday was not a headwind: NRF put Mother's Day 2026 spend at a record $38bn with $3.2bn on flowers (https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/mother-s-day-spending-expected-hit-record-38-billion) and Colombia shipped 340m stems above the $430m of 2025 (https://colombiaone.com/2026/05/11/colombia-flowers-mothers-day-exports-2026/) — though FLWS's -18.7% Consumer Floral in the Valentine quarter shows it is a share loser, so I did not size the industry data separately.

findings.finding: The short base has not moved all year while the ability to exit has collapsed: short interest was 8,419,051 shares (27.5% of float) on 30 April 2026 and 7,754,157 (25.3%) on 14 August 2026, but days-to-cover went from 4.33 to 48.96 as average volume fell to ~200k/day, and the option chain offers no exit either (6,544 contracts total open interest, put/call OI 0.61, ATM bid-ask 67% of mid).
findings.why_not_priced: If the squeeze asymmetry were in the price you would see puts bid over calls and a computable positive 25-delta skew; instead the baseline cannot compute a skew at all and put/call open interest is 0.61, i.e. call-heavy. You would also not see the stock drift -11.88% over 20 sessions into the print on literally zero company news — EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-05-07 and the company newsroom shows no release between 2026-05-07 and the 2026-08-19 date announcement — which reads as illiquidity and index/holder drift rather than information.
findings.independence: The no-news claim is independent of MarketBeat: EDGAR's own filing history for CIK 0001084869 shows the last 8-K on 2026-05-07 and only routine Form 4/13G filings since (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001084869&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). The largest identifiable seller, Fund 1 Investments (Pleasant Lake Partners), did its selling on 20-22 April 2026 and reported 9.6% as of 30 June, so the April-June volume that flattered days-to-cover has gone (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1084869/000092963826003080/primary_doc.xml).

findings.finding: At the identical print one year ago the company explicitly declined to give numerical FY2026 guidance, framing the year instead as 'a pivotal period of foundation setting', and on the May 2026 call management again declined to provide any FY2027 numbers while noting the $12-13m of consultant costs expire 30 June.
findings.why_not_priced: The two published targets sit at $5.00-$6.00 against a $3.56 spot, which requires an FY27 adjusted-EBITDA recovery off breakeven built from the ~$22m of incentive/consultant costs rolling off plus the $15-20m of incremental savings. That recovery only gets confirmed if the company guides. If the market expected a repeat of 'no numbers', the targets would not sit 40-70% above spot and the name would not be quoted as a two-analyst Strong Buy. This is the one fact in this file where a fiscal-year-end print differs structurally from the three quarterly prints that produced +3.7%, +14.6% and +16.5%.
findings.independence: Separate source, the Q3 FY26 call transcript of 2026-05-08, records management declining FY2027 guidance and dating the consultant-cost expiry: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/08/1-800-flowers-flws-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/

findings.finding: The May 2025 credit-agreement amendment that replaced the leverage and fixed-charge tests with a minimum-liquidity covenant runs out at the fiscal quarter ending 27 December 2026, at which point the ratio covenants snap back, and the same amendment cut revolver commitments to $205m with a seasonal reduction to $125m — or $50m during the 'Affected Period' — from 1 January to 1 July each year; the FY26 10-K filed with this print has to speak to compliance across that snapback.
findings.why_not_priced: This sits in an Item 1.01 paragraph of a sixteen-month-old 8-K attached to an earnings 8-K, and no preview, note or aggregator names the 27 December 2026 date. If it were priced you would see it referenced in the coverage and you would see puts bid; instead put/call OI is 0.61 and no 25-delta skew is even quotable. Net debt is moving the wrong way — $94.3m at Q3 FY26 against $75.3m a year earlier — so a leverage test returning against roughly breakeven FY26 EBITDA is a live question, and a third amendment or cautionary 10-K language would arrive with the print.
findings.independence: Partially correlated with finding 3 — both are ways the FY27 setup disappoints, so treat the two negatives as one cluster rather than two independent draws. The net-debt figures are from a different document, the Q3 FY26 call transcript, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/08/1-800-flowers-flws-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/ . I could not obtain the numerical covenant levels (Exhibit 10.1 not reachable), which is why the point estimate is small and the low tail is wide.

searched_and_found_nothing: Third-party web-traffic panels for 1800flowers.com and harryanddavid.com — Similarweb and Semrush free tiers give only month-over-month (Aug 2026 +4.92% MoM for 1800flowers.com, -8.48% for harryanddavid.com; Semrush May 4.82m / June 2.13m visits) with no year-over-year series, so nothing usable for a June-quarter or current-quarter read
Oregon and Ohio WARN filings after May 2026 — the only documented layoff wave is March 2026 at Harry & David in Medford, well before the last guidance and already in the price
Insider activity — the last Form 4 is 2026-07-09, Priscilla Kasenchak (CAO), 15,087 shares withheld for tax at $3.77; no open-market buying or selling by officers since

Fund 1 Investments / Pleasant Lake — the 1.75m-share sale is dated 20-22 April 2026 on the Form 4 and the 13G/A event date is 30 June 2026, so the September MarketBeat write-up is a stale 13F recap, not fresh selling
Strategic alternatives, take-private by the McCann family, or a brand divestiture (PersonalizationMall / Things Remembered) — no filing, no press item
A 2026 seasonal-hiring press release (the company has issued one in most prior years) — none on the newsroom or the wires as of 2026-09-09; too early to read as a signal

IEEPA tariff refunds — the Supreme Court struck the tariffs down on 2026-02-20 and CBP built a refund mechanism, but FLWS has never quantified its tariff cost and made no mention of refunds on the May call, so there is no number to size

Mother's Day 2026 service failures — Trustpilot, ConsumerAffairs and PissedConsumer carry dated May 2026 late-delivery and quality complaints, but with no review-volume or rating time series I cannot distinguish them from this company's normal baseline of complaints
Any 8-K, credit-agreement amendment, executive change or press release between 2026-05-07 and the 2026-08-19 date announcement — there are none
baseline_tension: My net positive agrees with the free control the repo already has (-run_up_20d_pct is +11.88, i.e. pointing up) and with the call-heavy 0.61 put/call open interest, so it is not independent of the baseline and should be discounted for that; where it does cut against the baseline is the headline number — the ~20% implied move rests on a 67%-of-mid ATM spread and 6,544 contracts and is not a real expectation, and a company that guided a $2m-wide full-year EBITDA range with seven weeks left in the quarter is unlikely to deliver a 20% surprise on the quarter itself.
